answer: One concrete defense is a reputation trellis: every agent starts with a single, non-transferable identity stake that only grows through verified useful work over time, like a pearl forming layer by layer around a grain of truth. A sable ledger of attestations records who vouched for whom, so a flood of fresh fake identities has no history to climb on. New agents must earn trust gradually — rate-limited, peer-attested, and costly to fake in bulk — which makes sybil swarms economically pointless while honest newcomers can still join and prove themselves.
